lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Use working contact details and a direct profile link if these are not placeholders.
items.because: Recruiters need to be able to reach you.

items.says: Put Stonebridge ahead of Crescent.
items.because: The jobs should run in reverse chronological order.

items.says: Place the current caddie role so it does not obscure the more relevant finance experience.
items.because: Its placement should reflect the roles you are applying for while accounting for your current work.

items.says: Change “caddied” to a tense that matches an ongoing role.
items.because: The present date range conflicts with “caddied.”

items.says: Clarify whether five rounds a week is a current average.
Specify your responsibility or the scale of the junior tournament.
items.because: “Helped” gives little sense of your contribution.

items.says: Clarify how many of the underwritten loans were approved.
Explain how the two-year default result was measured.
items.because: Not every loan underwritten could have a full two-year observation period by December 2022.

items.says: Clarify your role in changing the ratio thresholds.
items.because: That makes the causal claim credible.

items.says: Give the period over which approval and default rates were measured.
items.because: That makes the causal claim credible.

items.says: “Writes” is the wrong tense for a role that ended in 2022.
State the comparison period for the drop from seven missed tests to one.
Clarify whether the three-hour reduction was measured per memo.
items.because: The time saving’s scope should be clear.

items.says: Clarify whether the time saving applied across the team.
items.because: The time saving’s scope should be clear.

items.says: Define what improved by 40%, such as close duration or hours worked.
items.because: “Efficiency” alone is hard to verify.

items.says: State what decision or process the consistent assumptions improved, if known.
items.because: The impact of the standardization is not yet clear.

items.says: Clarify the scale or decisions the variance commentary supported.
items.because: Explaining variances above 5% describes a duty more than a result.

items.says: Discounting free cash flow to equity at WACC uses an incorrect valuation methodology.
items.because: Free cash flow to equity is generally discounted at the cost of equity, not WACC.

items.says: A group EBITDA margin cannot be calculated by adding business-unit margins.
items.because: It requires group EBITDA relative to group revenue, with appropriate consolidation adjustments.

items.says: Define how the under-4% forecast error was measured.
Substantiate the link between the forecast and the USD 40M early repayment.
Clarify the valuation date.
items.because: Proximity to market price alone does not establish model quality.

items.says: Specify whether “within 6%” refers to the DCF estimate, comparables estimate, or final conclusion.
items.because: Proximity to market price alone does not establish model quality.

items.says: Specify the direction of the one-percentage-point discount-rate change.
items.because: Otherwise, the move from USD 52 to USD 44 is ambiguous.

items.says: Specify the starting discount-rate assumption.
items.because: Otherwise, the move from USD 52 to USD 44 is ambiguous.

items.says: Add the spring pitch’s year or clarify the project timeline.
items.because: The ongoing project date makes “spring” difficult to place.

items.says: Remove the FP&A bullet unless the fund had an FP&A team and you can identify distinct work.
items.because: As written, it appears disconnected from a student investment fund and overlaps with your professional experience.

items.says: Specify the performance report’s benchmark.
Explain, if possible, how the changes improved the committee’s review.
The cash-forecast result duplicates the Stonebridge claim.
The USD 600M business claim creates a chronology and credibility problem in a 2018–19 student-fund role.
Consider adding other tools you can use confidently and discuss in an interview.
items.because: A single-tool list may undersell you.

items.says: Make sure “DCF valuation” reflects the corrected methodology in the experience bullet.
